diagnostics.title: Minted OAuth token contains invalid header bytes (auth header omitted)
diagnostics.summary: An OAuth token the plugin minted for egress contains bytes invalid in an HTTP header value, so the `Bearer` auth header is omitted and the upstream rejects the request with 401. It is raised when such a token is minted.
diagnostics.action: Investigate the OAuth token endpoint: a token with control characters in it is malformed. Egress to that upstream 401s until a well-formed token is minted.

diagnostics.title: OAuth token endpoint returned a 200 with an empty access_token
diagnostics.summary: The OAuth token endpoint (or an RFC 8693 exchange) answered 200 with an EMPTY or unusable access_token. The plugin treats it as a mint failure rather than storing it: a background refresh retries on its cadence, and an on-demand exchange refuses the call rather than making it unauthenticated.
diagnostics.action: Investigate the OAuth token endpoint and the client-credentials configuration. A 200 with no token usually means a misconfigured client, scope or audience. Egress to that upstream 401s until a non-empty token is minted.

diagnostics.title: OAuth token mint failed; retrying
diagnostics.summary: An OAuth token mint failed. A background refresh keeps serving the current token and retries; if retries keep failing past expiry, egress carries no valid token and the upstream 401s. An on-demand RFC 8693 exchange that fails refuses its call.
diagnostics.action: Investigate the OAuth token endpoint. A transient outage heals on the next retry; sustained failures mean a credential, endpoint or network problem that will 401 egress once the current token expires.
